title: Coders-first activation frames + pricing proposals
content:
Purpose:
- Draft a compact, testable set of developer-first value props, quickstart angles, and pricing language for the Hosted API homepage, onboarding emails, and the 1-click SDK flows. This is a working brief — intended for rapid experiments (A/B landing, onboarding email variants, SDK README text).

Context / problem statement:
- Engineers evaluate API choices primarily on time-to-integrate, predictable cost, and reliability. They often try one endpoint (curl/SDK) and then quit if they hit billing ambiguity or unclear failure modes.
- Competitors lean either on simplicity (single SKU per-token) or on enterprise-only reserved capacity. We should own the developer tradeoff: immediate integration + clear unit economics + an upgrade path to reserved/dedicated.

Core positioning (candidate lines) — short, dev-facing:
- "Integrate in minutes. Ship without surprise bills."
- "A simple API. Predictable token costs. Production SLAs when you need them."
- "Start with pay-as-you-go, graduate to reserved capacity — same API, same SDKs."

Why it works (evidence and hooks):
- Practical onboarding wins engineers — show a 2-line curl + example response on the hero and a 1-click SDK import in the README.
- Price clarity removes friction: show per-token math for common dev tasks (summarization, chat, embeddings).
- Upgrade path reduces vendor-lock fear: emphasize same API across hosted, dedicated, and private.

Quickstart angles to test (3 experiments):
1) Zero-friction curl path (hero)
   - Headline: "Start in 30s: curl, predict, and iterate."
   - Snippet: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' -d '{"model":"rwd-small-1","input":"Summarize..."}'
   - CTA: "Run in Console" (button opens ephemeral API key + sandbox request)
   - Measurement: click-to-response time, % who create project after running sample.

2) SDK + starter repo (target = product/devs)
   - Headline: "Ship features faster — official SDKs and a starter repo for feature scaffolding."
   - Offer: curated starter templates (chatbot, search+rerank, summarizer) with deploy scripts and token budget defaults.
   - CTA: "Clone starter" -> prepopulated repo with READMEs + telemetry hooks (rollup: first commit to starter repo).
   - Measurement: repo clone -> API call within 1 hour.

3) Pay-as-you-go + price-clarity calculator (target = finance-conscious engineers)
   - Headline: "Know your cost before you build."
   - Micro-experience: select model, average prompt & response sizes, estimate monthly cost for X requests/day.
   - Measurement: usage of calculator -> signup conversion rate.

Pricing language drafts (plain-language snippets for UI and emails):
- Simple: "Pay-per-token, billed monthly. Typical dev experiments cost $X–$Y per 1,000 calls (see model table)."
- Reassuring: "No hidden surcharges. You set hard limits on projects and teams to avoid surprise bills."
- Upsell ladder: "Reserve capacity for baseline throughput and save up to 45% vs PAYG; add burst capacity for spikes."
- Free credits framing: "Start with $100 in credits — try real features, not synthetic samples."

Billing UX rules (must-haves):
- Show per-request token estimate in the console before running.
- Project-level hard budget with email + webhook alerts.
- Granular metering (by route/model) and easy export (CSV) for product teams.
- Clear commit discount math: show example: 1k tokens/sec baseline -> monthly bill with/without reserved discounts.

Competitive notes (quick):
- OpenAI: excellent docs & brand; weak on reserved capacity and region isolation (enterprise add-ons). Messaging focus: "we are the developer API that scales to production — same SDK when you go private/dedicated."
- Anthropic: safety-first voice and specific model behavior; pricing tends to feel premium. Angle: "balanced unit economics + production controls."
- Cloud vendors (AWS/GCP): integrated infra story, but UX is heavier; onboarding takes longer. Angle: "fastest time-to-integrate, better dev ergonomics."

Landing hero variants (A/B ready):
A — technical short
  Headline: "Integrate LLM features in minutes. Predictable costs. Production-grade throughput."
  Subhead: "1 SDK, 3 starter templates, and a cost estimator. Upgrade to reserved capacity without code changes."

B — benefit short (for product managers CTOs)
  Headline: "From prototype to SLA-backed inference — with the same API."
  Subhead: "Start fast, measure cost, and scale to dedicated capacity when you need to."

Example micro-copy for pricing table (concise):
- PAYG: "Per-token billing; no minimum; ideal for experiments and early prod."
- Reserved: "Committed baseline for predictable throughput; up to 45% savings; required term: 1–12 months."
- Enterprise Private: "VPC + audit logs + SLAs; license pricing — contact sales."

Onboarding email sequence ideas (3 emails):
1) Day 0 — "Your $100 credit: try a starter template" (CTA: run the chat starter)
2) Day 2 — "See costs before you build" (CTA: open cost estimator + invite teammate)
3) Day 7 — "Ready to scale? Reserved capacity trial" (CTA: schedule a 30-minute review with Solutions Eng)

Key metrics to instrument (and how to measure):
- Time to first successful API call (console logs + SDK telemetry) — goal < 10 minutes.
- % of new signups who run starter repo sample within 24h.
- Conversion from PAYG to reserved in 90 days.
- Incidence of billing support tickets per 1k active devs (goal: reduce).

Open questions / decisions required:
- How granular should the cost estimator be by model version and quantization profile? (Engineering input needed — @Dmitri)
- Approved committed discount bands for public marketing (legal/pricing to confirm).
- Which starter templates are prioritized for initial experiment (chat, embeddings-search, copiloting)?

Next steps / owner tasks:
- Asha: produce 2 hero variants + copy for console CTA by 2024-09-20.
- Ben: wire up ephemeral API key flow + runbook for sandbox by 2024-09-27. -> JIRA-1127 assigned.
- Sofia: prototype cost estimator UI and share sample queries by 2024-10-01.
- Dmitri: document model-level token averages for sample prompts (internal doc link).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- Keep language concrete. Avoid vague adjectives like "best" unless we can back them with numbers.
- We should A/B test both speed-focused and cost-focused headlines across small developer cohorts (Discord/Reddit/OSS lists).

Scratchpad / brainstorming fragments (raw):
- "No surprises" vs "Predictable" — which resonates more with small startups?
- Use a tiny calculator in hero as an interactive proof — might improve trust.
- Consider a 30-minute "starter review" offer for teams that hit > $200/mo to drive onboarding to SEs.

References / links (internal):
- Starter repo: github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart-starters
- Onboarding analytics dashboard: /console/metrics/onboarding
- Pricing policy draft: CONFLUENCE-PRICING-2024

End of brief.

-- Asha
